## Historical audit: S0055

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/quota_restored_20261103/retired/results/r1/generic_rsi/C1/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`.

| Evidence | Observation |
|---|---|
| JSONL line 1, `model_request`, student, characters [0,10098) | The requested goal was to reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, occlusion, colors and materials. The image was supplied by path, but its contents are not visible in this audit. The instructions required an initial complete build and render-based review. |
| Line 2, `codex_session`, student, [0,2623) | One fresh, read-only CLI session was launched with an image. It failed with exit code 1 after approximately 14.75 seconds; zero tool calls were recorded. The actual model and underlying inference-round count are unknown. |
| Line 3, `model_error`, student, [0,544); line 4, `scene_error`, [0,1606) | The failure propagated through the model call and scene loop. The error points to a stderr log, whose contents are not included. |

**Outcome and changes.** This is a **technical interruption**, not evidence of formal success, partial geometric correctness, or an algorithmic reconstruction failure. No scene program, executed build, patch, render, revision, or validation is visible. An empty patch is not established; rather, no patch is shown. No autonomous exploration is recorded. No teacher input or student adoption is visible; the student system instructions are not evidence of teacher feedback.

**Scene-specific uncertainty.** The request calls for multiple objects and separate meshes, but the unseen photograph does not establish which objects or textures are present. No constructed materials, part connections, object poses, camera, lighting, or render can be assessed. There is likewise no visible teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or execution. The CLI exit is established, but its underlying cause remains unresolved without the referenced stderr.

**Lessons.** Transferably, distinguish a failed model session from a failed reconstruction algorithm, and require an actual render before judging scene quality. The particular reference scene, its geometric discrepancies, and any corrective choices remain task-specific unknowns.
